title: Double bass
summary: Open strings only (E1, A1, D2, G2), on a computed shell body that keeps its lowest 256 modes, to 1623.5 Hz: above that the body neither moves nor radiates, so the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. Stopped notes have recordings but no render yet. The body is spruce and maple shell with a 116 L air cavity through the f-holes, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route, not a scan; wood below 150 Hz is a declared extrapolation. Strings are Thomastik Spirocore with no printed loss. The bow is a 10 mm ribbon with hair compliance on the measured rosin curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13). The after-length is a sixth of the speaking length (E1) or a sixth x 116/115 (A1, D2, G2), a ratio borrowed from the cello.
physics_present: computed double-bass shell body: spruce top and bass bar, maple back, ribs and bridge, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route; the lowest 256 modes are kept, ending at 1623.5 Hz; first structural mode 106 Hz
air cavity of 116 L breathing through the f-holes (a physical neck); coupled air mode 61 Hz
wood from the measured spruce (from 100 Hz) and maple (from 150 Hz) packs, with the lower band edge moved to 90 Hz as a declared extrapolation, not a measurement
Thomastik Spirocore Orchestra 4/4 medium strings (maker's tension table, line mass and gauges) at a 1.100 m speaking length, bending modes in two polarisations, with a bending stiffness
bow of finite width: a 10 mm ribbon of 3 cells with hair compliance (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998)
friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13), a steady sliding curve
static compliance of the omitted body modes at the bridge and under the bow (exact static Green)
after-length (bridge to tailpiece): one sixth of the speaking length (E1) or one sixth x 116/115 (A1, D2, G2), the printed bowed-string rule with the cello's 116 mm ratio borrowed
a bow gesture on a fixed schedule: a 0.15 s ramp to the note's force at 0.15 m/s, then a 20 ms lift; each page states its bow force
physics_missing: body modes above the 256th: the pages keep the binary's limit when they were rendered, so above 1623.5 Hz the body neither moves nor radiates and the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up
stopped notes: the pages are open strings only; Eb2, D3 and Db4 have recordings and no render

a measured bass: the body is mapped from a maker's published specification onto the il Cannone specimen tables, not scanned; the bass bar is moved 18.1 mm inward to clear the f-hole (no source prints that position); the bridge is a uniform 152.6 g shell; the 1.070 m of a 3/4 instrument is not modelled
measured wood properties below 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce)
string loss: none is printed for these strings, so the cards carry none and the notes ring on after the bow lifts
string torsion: the cards carry no twist modes
the rosin's temperature and contact history: the friction is a steady sliding curve with no thermal or third-body memory
a printed double-bass after-length: the 116/115 ratio is borrowed from the cello
player variation: bow speed and force follow a fixed schedule
blocked: Stopped notes (Eb2, D3, Db4 are recording-only): no finger-stop render is posted yet; the route is still being tested.
